name: Multicast networking
plain: Sends and receives multicast and broadcast traffic on the local network.
meaning: Needed for custom device discovery; also a way to enumerate LAN devices, so Apple gates it by approval.

android.prompt_ui: None (Android 17 local network permission also applies)
android.note: Android 17 treats multicast and broadcast as local network traffic

ios.prompt_ui: Apple request form; local network prompt also applies
ios.note: Bonjour is exempt; raw multicast and broadcast need the entitlement

limits.headline: Can send and receive shared messages to many devices on your local network
limits.user_action: Nothing, or you use device discovery or casting inside the app
can: Listen for broadcast announcements on the local network
Find devices that announce themselves (printers, TVs)
Use raw multicast on iPhone with the Apple entitlement
Use Bonjour on iPhone with no extra entitlement
cannot: Use raw multicast on iPhone without the Apple entitlement
Skip local network rules on Android 17
Listen for free on Android; a multicast lock costs battery
limits.differs: iPhone exempts Bonjour but needs an entitlement for raw multicast. Android needs a normal permission and treats multicast as local traffic in Android 17.

story.what_it_is: An app sends and gets messages to many devices at once on your local network.

marketing.name: Multicast entitlement
marketing.pitch: Apple requires special approval before apps can use multicast and broadcast on a local network.

story.for_you: You do not see it. It is how your phone finds a smart speaker or a game host without typing an address. If an app uses it for scanning, it can see devices on the whole network.
story.for_makers: Makers use it for fast discovery of nearby devices. Apple limits it because it can also be used to scan every device. Apps ask for approval and explain their reason.

use_cases.example: A music or TV app announces itself on the network to find speakers.
A local multiplayer game finds hosts on the same Wi-Fi without a server.
A setup app broadcasts a message so a new device answers.
A company tool finds printers and displays in the office.
A developer uses it to find test devices on a lab network.
A bad app sends discovery packets to map every device in a house.

story.android_note: Android apps need a multicast lock and can use it with the normal network permissions.
story.ios_note: iPhone needs a special entitlement from Apple that apps must request.

technical_bounds: Both platforms add local network prompts

history.change: Multicast entitlement required for raw multicast and broadcast
Multicast counted as local network access
